tier_reason: The README Performance section has IPA/Wiki/Distinct/Url tables with xcdat<8> 826 vs marisa 1818 ns/key lookup and 1173 vs 1515 ns/id decode on Wiki, xcdat<15> 619 ns/key, and Url 469 vs 1789 ns/key, all matching the record. The benchmark code is public at kampersanda/fast_succinct_trie/bench (bench.cpp, CMakeLists.txt, marisa-trie and xcdat submodules), and the README states AppleClang 12.0.0, -O3 -march=native and a MacBook Pro 13-inch 2019 with a 2.4 GHz quad-core Core i5. That machine identifies the CPU closely enough, as with earlier 'MacBook Pro 16-inch 2019, 2.4 GHz Core i9' A precedents.

corrections.caveats: The baseline is marisa-trie, not SDSL or sux, so this is a trie-dictionary win rather than a bitvector or wavelet-tree win. xcdat is faster than the succinct tries (marisa, tx, fst, pdt) but slower than the plain double-array tries (darts-clone 450 ns/key on Wiki) and hat-trie (368 ns/key), and it uses about twice marisa's memory (139 vs 69 MiB on Wiki). It ran on a laptop Core i5 with only the AppleClang toolchain; the SKU number is not printed, only 'MacBook Pro (13-inch, 2019), 2.4 GHz Quad-Core Intel Core i5'. The benchmark code is in the sibling repo kampersanda/fast_succinct_trie/bench, not in xcdat. dastrie did not complete its build on the Distinct dataset. xcdat was compared directly with a succinct-trie incumbent, not with std containers.

notes: All numbers check out. The comparison table also shows that the double-array competitors look up faster but use 3-8x the memory, so the claim holds only within the compact-trie class; the caveats now say so. Last commit is 2024-09-10 (stale), MIT, and the repo is neither archived nor a fork.

corrections.claimed_speedup: No numbers on the repo page. The Algorithmica 2019 paper (Gog, Karkkainen, Kempa, Petri, Puglisi) is cited for the experiments; its abstract, seen only as a search snippet, says the new FM-indexes are 'consistently fast and small relative to the state-of-the-art'. No ratio against SDSL has been seen.
corrections.caveats: This is wt_fbb, an SDSL-compatible wavelet tree class with no benchmark scripts in the repo. The win over SDSL is unverified because the Algorithmica paper (arXiv 1104.3810 is the SPIRE 2011 conference version) could not be opened. Retier when arXiv or Springer is reachable; B is likely if the paper's count/locate tables beat SDSL FM-indexes. Third-party follow-ups ('Another Virtue of Wavelet Forests', SPIRE 2024; 'Wavelet Forests Revisited', arXiv 2604.11338) study the same fixed-block-boosting wavelet forests; the latter reports, per snippet only, up to 2x faster queries than standalone optimized wavelet trees with RRR bitvectors. A search snippet's 'up to 2x access/select, 3x rank vs SDSL' figure belongs to Kurpicz's 'Faster Wavelet Tree Queries', a different project, and must not be attributed here. The repo has 2 commits; the last is 2021-05-18.
